[vanyellow] please start buying ddr5 to test this theory for us
and some nvme 2tb ssds
[pongky] When I built my current PC in 2020 I used ddr4 ram — genuinely asking, is ddr4 still relevant today? compatible with new mobos?
[cycleri3] No but AI is buying all DDR5 so your gonna pay much more to buy that.
[TheFool] It depends. For new builds DDR5 is of course better but for existing builds, DDR4 is still a great choice, especially the considering DDR5 prices today.
[Agret] With the price of DDR5 it might be better to build with DDR4 even if you have to use an older generation CPU to run it. Depends on budget of course.
[boozed] It's compatible with Intel LGA1700 which is only previous gen, so not obsolete yet
[Pyrock] Due to the absurd price increases of ddr5, the used market for all the hardware that supports ddr4 has been pretty busy.
Manufacturers have even been extending hardware lines and even releasing new lines of the old hardware supporting ddr4
So yes, absolutely relevant today and compatible with mobos that are running last gen components (but still sold new) but not compatible with current gen newer hardware
